clues: This city stands on the bank of the Potomac River. Maryland wraps it on the north, east, and south.
Summers are hot and damp, and heat with damp air brings storms again and again. Winters are chilly, and a big blizzard can strike every few years.
In 1790, a law chose a site by the Potomac for a capital district of its own. In 1800, Congress moved here from Philadelphia and took its seat.
A designer drew this whole capital on paper in 1791 before its streets were built. The White House, home of the president, has stood here since 1800.
This city is the seat of rule for the United States. The Supreme Court and the main offices of the land are here too.
